embedding.title: Vector Embeddings
embedding.description: Enable semantic search against your wiki. Works with OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoints and Google Gemini native embedContent endpoints. Local models (LM Studio, Ollama embedding) don't need an API key.
embedding.enableHint: When off, search uses token matching only.
embedding.endpointHint: OpenAI-compatible example: http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/embeddings. Gemini example: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta with model gemini-embedding-001.
embedding.outputDimensionalityHint: Optional. Sent only for Gemini native embedContent endpoints as `output_dimensionality`; OpenAI-compatible endpoints ignore this field. Leave empty for the model default. Rebuild embeddings after changing model or dimension.
embedding.extraHeadersHint: Optional. One per line, formatted `Header-Name: value`. Used for gateways that route by request header — e.g. mify needs `X-Model-Provider-Id: siliconflow`. Authorization, Content-Type, Host, Content-Length, and x-goog-api-key are managed by the client and will be ignored.
embedding.maxChunkCharsHint: Target size of each chunk. Lower this (e.g. 500) when your endpoint's context is small (llama.cpp n_ctx=512, mxbai-embed-large, etc.).
embedding.overlapChunkCharsHint: Characters of overlap between adjacent chunks so ideas aren't severed at boundaries.
embedding.providerTestsHint: Connection test sends one short embedding request. Functional test verifies stable finite vectors and reports the returned dimension.
embedding.legacyPromptBody: Your project has {{count}} entries in the old per-page vector store. The new per-chunk index gives better retrieval but needs a one-time re-embed. Run "Re-index all pages" to upgrade.

multimodal.title: Vision / Image OCR
multimodal.description: Configure the vision LLM. Used for two things: (1) when you paste / drop / import images into chat or sources, the model extracts content as markdown (description + verbatim OCR) for the wiki; (2) when ingesting PDFs / DOCX / PPTX, the same model captions embedded images for semantic search. Captions are cached by image SHA-256 — duplicate logos only call the LLM once.
multimodal.enableHint: Off: (1) uploaded images keep only the original file, no OCR/description; (2) embedded images in PDFs/DOCX get no captions. On: each new image triggers one vision-LLM call (cached by hash). If your main LLM is text-only, disable 'Use main LLM' below and configure a vision-capable endpoint here.
multimodal.useMainHint: Reuse the model picked under Settings → LLM provider. Only enable this if that model accepts image input — text-only models will return a 400.
multimodal.customEndpointHint: OpenAI-compatible /v1 base. LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, LocalAI all work.
multimodal.azureEndpointHint: Use your Azure OpenAI resource endpoint. The model field is the deployment name.
multimodal.azureApiVersionHint: Sent as the Azure OpenAI api-version query parameter.
multimodal.azureModelFamilyHint: Choose GPT-5 / o-series if this deployment rejects max_tokens or non-default temperature.
multimodal.apiKeyPlaceholder: Leave blank for local / no-auth endpoints
multimodal.modelHint: Must be a vision-capable model. Text-only models will fail with a 400 / image-not-supported error at first ingest.
multimodal.concurrencyHint: How many caption requests run in parallel. 1 = strictly sequential. 4 is a good default for most setups; raise to 8+ only on a beefy GPU or hosted endpoint.
multimodal.costPoint1: Each new image triggers one vision-LLM call (~500-2000 tokens depending on model + thinking mode).
multimodal.costPoint2: Captions are cached by SHA-256 of image bytes. Duplicate logos / shared chart templates across documents only ever incur ONE call.
multimodal.costPoint3: Rust-side filter drops images smaller than 100×100 px and caps at 500 images per source — pathological PDFs can't blow up the bill.
multimodal.costPoint4: Prefer a local vision model (Qwen2.5-VL via LM Studio / Ollama) for bulk ingestion; reserve hosted vision APIs for one-off high-stakes documents.

apiServer.title: API Server
apiServer.description: A local HTTP API at 127.0.0.1:19828 exposes project files, search, graph, and rescan to your own scripts and tools. Bind your favorite editor or shell to read the wiki without going through the UI.
apiServer.enableHint: Disable to make every non-/health endpoint return 503 even if a token is configured. Useful as a kill-switch without unsetting the token.
apiServer.openHealthHint: Opens in your system browser. /health is the only unauthenticated endpoint.
apiServer.allowUnauthenticatedHint: Use only for trusted local agents. Any process or browser page on this machine can call the API while this is enabled.
apiServer.tokenHint: Required unless unauthenticated access is enabled. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `X-LLM-Wiki-Token: <token>`. The environment variable LLM_WIKI_API_TOKEN overrides this field if set.
apiServer.tokenPlaceholder: Paste an existing token or click Generate
apiServer.tokenMissing: No token — every endpoint will return 401
apiServer.tokenUnused: Token is not used while unauthenticated access is enabled
apiServer.envTokenActive: LLM_WIKI_API_TOKEN is active and overrides this field
apiServer.tokenWeak: Token is short — consider Generate for 256-bit entropy
apiServer.saveFirst: Save settings to apply API changes
apiServer.saveFirstExample: Save settings first, then copy an example request.
apiServer.tokenWarning: Keep this token secret. Anyone with the token on this machine can read your project files via localhost.
apiServer.tokenQueryWarning: Prefer the Authorization header — passing ?token=… via URL leaks the value into shell history, logs, and Referer headers.
apiServer.endpointsHint: Replace {id} with a project UUID, a project filesystem path, or the literal 'current'.
apiServer.endpointProjectsNote: List known projects with their IDs and paths.
apiServer.endpointSearchNote: JSON body: { query, topK?, includeContent?, queryEmbedding? }. Uses shared keyword + vector retrieval when embeddings are configured.
apiServer.endpointRescanNote: Triggers a backend rescan using your Source Watch config.

labs.title: Labs (Experimental)
labs.description: Features that aren't validated for general use yet. Opt in if you want to help shake them out; opt out anytime — your data and settings are unaffected.
labs.agentIngestHint: Shows a 🤖 button next to each source file. A multi-turn LLM agent reads the source via tool calls (read_chunk / search_source) and writes wiki pages (write_wiki_page / update_wiki_page) — vs the classic single-shot analyse + generate pipeline. Costs more tokens. Quality not yet validated on long real-world docs; uncovered topics surface as Review items.
labs.aiLintFixHint: Replaces the lint Fix button's hardcoded actions (orphan → append to index.md, broken-link → push to Review) with an LLM mini-agent that decides per-item how to repair the wiki — fixing the link, cross-linking the orphan to topic-adjacent pages, adding wikilinks to a no-outlinks page. Costs LLM tokens per click; falls back to classic fix if the agent fails.
labs.chatAgentHint: Upgrades chat from a single-turn stream into a tool-calling agent. When the LLM needs info it can call web_fetch (any URL, zero config), web_search (your configured Tavily / SerpApi / SearXNG / Ollama), search_local_files (project-scoped), and wiki inspection tools. Costs more tokens and drops the per-token streaming UX in agent mode — the first response arrives as a complete block once the agent finishes its tool calls.
labs.chatAgentCanWriteLabel: Chat agent can write wiki pages (experimental)
labs.chatAgentCanWriteHint: Adds write_wiki_page + update_wiki_page to the chat agent's tools. Use this when you want the agent to create / update pages directly from chat ("save this as a wiki page", "update concepts/foo with this"). The prompt rails it to write ONLY when you explicitly ask. delete + link tools are NOT included — those stay in ingest / lint-fix paths. Requires Chat agent ON.
labs.chatAgentCanWriteParentOff: Enable Chat agent first to use this sub-flag.
labs.rawSaveToWikiLabel: Raw Save to Wiki — skip wikify rewrite
labs.rawSaveToWikiHint: By default, Save to Wiki sends the chat reply through a short LLM rewrite that strips conversational tone ("Based on...", "Here's a summary...") before writing the page. Turn this on to skip that pass and persist the reply verbatim — useful for record-keeping, code-heavy answers, or content where the rewrite over-edits. autoIngest and raw source preservation continue to run either way.
labs.disclaimer: Labs features may change shape, lose toggle state, or be removed without a version bump. They are NOT covered by the auto-update's compatibility guarantees.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.description: Tools for cleaning up the wiki — detect and merge duplicate entities/concepts that the LLM created under different names across re-ingests.

dedup.title: Detect duplicate entities / concepts
dedup.description: Asks the LLM to scan all entity / concept pages and group ones that likely refer to the same topic under different names (English vs Chinese, plural vs singular, abbreviation vs full form). You confirm each group before merging. Merges are queued and run one at a time so cross-references stay consistent.
dedup.noneFound: No duplicate groups found. The wiki is clean.
dedup.queueDescription: Tasks queued from a previous scan that haven't finished yet. Merges run one at a time.

storageLocation.title: Storage Location
storageLocation.description: Detects whether the current project lives on local disk, a cloud sync folder, or a network share (SMB / AFP / NFS), and gives setup hints for that storage type.
storageLocation.noProject: Open or create a project first — storage detection runs against the project path.
storageLocation.watchWarningTitle: Source Watch won't fire reliably on network mounts
storageLocation.watchWarningBody: FSEvents / inotify / ReadDirectoryChangesW don't watch SMB / AFP / NFS paths. To keep auto-ingest working, use a NAS-vendor sync client (Synology Drive, fnOS Drive, Qsync) that syncs the share to a real local path, then point the project at that local path instead.
storageLocation.excludeDescription: .llm-wiki-local/ holds your personal chat history. Don't sync it — it produces conflict files across devices and leaks private conversations.

local.label: Local disk
local.subtitle: Lives on this device's filesystem. No sync involved.

icloud.label: iCloud Drive
icloud.subtitle: Synced via iCloud. Add .nosync suffix to exclude chat history.

dropbox.label: Dropbox
dropbox.subtitle: Synced via Dropbox. Use xattr to ignore .llm-wiki-local/.

synologyDrive.label: Synology Drive
synologyDrive.subtitle: Synced to a Synology NAS via the Drive Client.

fnosDrive.label: fnOS Drive
fnosDrive.subtitle: Synced to a fnOS (FeiNiu) NAS via the fnOS Drive client.

qsync.label: QNAP Qsync
qsync.subtitle: Synced to a QNAP NAS via the Qsync client.

terrasync.label: TerraMaster Sync
terrasync.subtitle: Synced to a TerraMaster NAS via TerraSync.

smb.label: SMB / CIFS share
smb.subtitle: Mounted network share. Source Watch won't fire here.

afp.subtitle: Legacy Apple Filing Protocol mount. SMB is recommended instead.

nfs.label: NFS share
nfs.subtitle: Mounted NFS export. Source Watch won't fire here.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.subtitle: Couldn't classify this path's storage type — treat as local.

schemaUpgrade.title: Schema Upgrade
schemaUpgrade.description: Replace this project's schema.md with the new comprehensive taxonomy (34 categories: travel, manuals, books, recipes, code, etc.). Future imports will route to the new directories.
schemaUpgrade.point1: Backs up the current schema.md to schema.md.bak-YYYY-MM-DD
schemaUpgrade.point2: Overwrites schema.md with the comprehensive template (in your current UI language)
schemaUpgrade.point3: Pre-creates the 34 category directories under wiki/
schemaUpgrade.point4: Leaves existing wiki pages where they are — does NOT auto-classify them
schemaUpgrade.warningBody: Pages currently under wiki/entities/, wiki/concepts/, wiki/sources/ stay where they are. Future imports use the new directories. To migrate old pages, delete the ingest cache and re-import the source documents.
schemaUpgrade.alreadyComprehensive: Already on the comprehensive schema — no action needed.
schemaUpgrade.notFound: schema.md not found in this project.
schemaUpgrade.success: Upgrade complete. Old schema.md saved as a backup; new categories ready.

configBackup.title: Config Backup
configBackup.description: Back up and restore all settings — including API keys. Exports are encrypted with your password (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM); the password is the only way to decrypt them.
configBackup.passwordHint: Remember this password — there is no recovery. It's needed to import on another machine.
configBackup.pwTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
configBackup.restartHint: Imported config takes effect after restart.
configBackup.autoDesc: On every launch the app writes an encrypted backup (key held in the OS keychain) to a stable folder, and auto-restores it on a fresh install — so a reinstall keeps your settings.
configBackup.securityNote: The exported file contains your API keys, encrypted. Anyone with the file AND the password can read them. Store both safely; the auto-backup's key lives in your OS keychain and never leaves this machine.
